verdict.rationale: Sketch documents its own official JavaScript API, described as fully supported between releases with browsable classes and methods. It also documents a sketchtool CLI, a sketch:// URL scheme, and a built-in local-only MCP server that lets AI clients interact with Sketch. However, the JS API runs inside the Mac app as plugins, and probes found no OpenAPI or public web API, so external programmatic driving is limited. Missing for 10: a documented public remote/web (REST) API or OpenAPI spec, a full API reference within the evidence, and independent hands-on corroboration of driving Sketch programmatically.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: An official vanilla JavaScript API, fully supported between releases. Browse all classes and methods, or drop down to the internal API when needed.
Write a Sketch plugin in JavaScript. Take advantage of ES6, access macOS frameworks and use the Sketch APIs without learning Objective-C or Swift.
Create assets with a single command with the Sketch command-line interface `sketchtool`.
Sketch includes a built-in MCP Server, a lightweight local-only web server that lets AI clients like ChatGPT or Claude interact directly with Sketch.
